_readme: Written settings with the location theme each one should resolve to.
The keyword table has been changed by hand repeatedly, and twice a change
had to be reverted because it broke a setting nobody was checking
('scavenger', 'after the collapse'). The sweep that caught both was run ad
hoc and never committed. This file is that gate.
setting        the world_style / idea text as a player would write it
expected       the theme id it SHOULD resolve to
allowed        for ambiguous entries: the set of defensible answers;
expected is ignored and membership in this list is asserted
known_failing  true when the code gets this wrong today. The test asserts
it still fails, so the corpus can record the truth without
being authored around the bug. Flipping one of these to
passing is a code fix, and the flag comes off in that commit.
note           why the expectation is what it is, where that is a judgement
tools/test_start_location_offline_theme.js, so the Python table and the JS
mirror in static/app.js are judged against one corpus.

settings.setting: a dying king and three heirs circling the throne
a mage academy where the youngest student is the strongest
knights and ruins on a road nobody maintains
mythic bronze age heroes and river gods
a village that pays its tithe to the dragon on the hill
low fantasy mercenary work, no chosen ones
elves and dwarves have not spoken in two hundred years
a peasant boy finds a sword in the reeds
a sect outer disciple grinding qi for a chance at the inner court
cultivation world where every breakthrough draws heavenly lightning
settings.note: Resolves celestial. 'heavenly' is xianxia's most common adjective and it matches the celestial keyword 'heaven', which is tested before fantasy. A cultivation world should not open in the afterlife.

settings.setting: wuxia jianghu, rival schools and one stolen manual
space opera, five empires and a missing heir
hard sci-fi orbital station running out of water
far-future interstellar civilisation with faster-than-light travel
colony ship mutiny in the second decade
a generation ship three hundred years from landfall
settings.note: 'colony ship' is a keyword and 'generation ship' is not. Candidate kw-1.

settings.setting: terraforming crew wakes up early and the atmosphere is wrong
first contact goes badly on a survey world
a derelict hauler drifting past the third moon
settings.note: Names no genre word at all. Unreachable by keywords on purpose -- WF2 territory. A placeless name is a visible miss; a wrong-genre name is a bug.

settings.setting: neon megacity where the corps own the rain
a netrunner with a burned-out deck and one favour left
near-future arcology, chrome and bad debt
a courier with a cranial shunt and bad debts
settings.note: Reads cyberpunk to a human and names nothing a table can match. WF2 territory; do not chase it with keywords.

settings.setting: post-apocalyptic convoy crossing the ashland
irradiated ruins and a working water chip
post-collapse settlement trading scrap for grain
after the collapse of the old empire, the roads are unsafe
settings.note: A fantasy sentence. Bare 'collapse' was tried as a wasteland keyword and reverted for exactly this. Must stay out of wasteland.

settings.setting: a frontier town with one law and no lawman
settings.note: A western. 'frontier' is a fantasy keyword, so it lands there. A timber-arch gate reads acceptably for a frontier town, so this is recorded ambiguous rather than treated as a bug -- removing 'frontier' would move real fantasy settings.

settings.setting: cattle drive gone wrong on the high plains
settings.note: No western bank exists. Generic is the correct answer, not a miss.

settings.setting: a roman legion posting on a cold frontier
settings.note: Same 'frontier' hit as above. Recorded, not fixed.

settings.setting: a haunted manor that rearranges its own corridors
vampire blood court politics in a rain-black city
a crypt beneath the chapel that was bricked up for a reason
cosmic horror in a fishing village nobody visits
settings.note: There is no horror bank. Generic is correct.

settings.setting: hardboiled detective, prohibition era, one missing dancer
a gumshoe takes a case he already knows is rigged
masked vigilantes in a city that resents them
settings.note: Superhero. No bank; the fantasy default is what used to open these at a gate-town.

settings.setting: a support hero who cannot fight but always arrives first
high school slice of life with a supernatural secret
a bakery on a busy street and the rival across the road
an office comedy about expense reports
small town summer, three friends, one broken bicycle
sengoku era retainer politics
age of sail privateering in the southern trade lanes
pirate voyage between trade islands
undersea dome city with a failing pressure seal
abyssal trench expedition that finds something
arctic research station, the sun will not rise for a month
a glacier crossing with too little rope
caravan across the sand sea between two oases
badlands salt flat where the wells are political
the heavens judge the newly dead in a court of light
an afterlife bureaucracy with a very long queue
airship privateers over a gaslamp capital
clockwork automata and a brass-plated parliament
a world with no magic at all, only steel and debt
settings.note: Negation strip. 'no magic' must not count as a magic signal.

settings.setting: grounded political drama, no fantasy elements whatsoever
a locksmith picking a stubborn lock in a modern city
settings.note: The 'picking' -> 'king' trap. Word-start anchoring fixed it; this keeps it fixed.

settings.setting: an industrial sector where the machines never stop
settings.note: 'sector' still reads as 'sect'. The word-start anchor guards the left of a keyword only, so a keyword may run into the middle of a longer word.

settings.setting: a heist crew casing a museum
someone wakes up and does not recognise their own hands
a letter arrives that should have been delivered forty years ago
two rivals inherit the same failing business
